findings.problem: The proof that the mean-distance profile y ↦ ∫ x, dist (F x) (F y) ∂μ is continuous is written inline. It packages (p.1,p.2) ↦ dist (F p.2) (F p.1) as a `C(S × S, ℝ)`, curries it, and composes with `continuous_integral_compact_function`. `exists_set_mean_approximation` in CompactSetMeanApproximation.lean (which imports this file) repeats the same `let d` and composition. Because it only proves continuity of the sum `obj n`, it then needs four more lines (`(ho n).sub hd`, `change`, `simpa … add_sub_cancel_right`) to get back the continuity this file already proved.
findings.proposed_change:
Add a lemma to this file, before the two theorems:

```lean
theorem continuous_integral_dist_profile
    {S Y : Type*} [TopologicalSpace S] [CompactSpace S]
    [MeasurableSpace S] [BorelSpace S] [PseudoMetricSpace Y]
    (F : S → Y) (hF : Continuous F) (μ : ProbabilityMeasure S) :
    Continuous (fun y => ∫ x, dist (F x) (F y) ∂(μ : Measure S)) := by
  let d : C(S × S, ℝ) := ⟨fun p => dist (F p.2) (F p.1),
    (hF.comp continuous_snd).dist (hF.comp continuous_fst)⟩
  exact (continuous_integral_compact_function μ).comp d.curry.continuous
```

The proof sketch is the target's current lines 23–26 with `μ n` generalized to `μ`. Rewritten uses:
(1) In `exists_deterministic_profile_centers`, delete `let d` and `hmean`, and write
`exists_le_integral ((continuous_integral_dist_profile F hF (μ n)).integrable_of_hasCompactSupport (HasCompactSupport.of_compactSpace _))`.
(2) In `exists_set_mean_approximation`, which has the same instances plus `T2Space`: `ho n` becomes `(continuous_integral_dist_profile F hF (μ n)).add hd`, with no local `d`. The `hc` block (lines 40–43, `(ho n).sub hd` / `change` / `simpa only [obj, add_sub_cancel_right]`) becomes `have hc := continuous_integral_dist_profile F hF (μ n)`.
findings.benefit: The continuity argument (curried continuous map plus continuity of integration in the uniform norm) gets one name and one proof, instead of two hand-built `C(S × S, ℝ)` packagings that must be kept in sync. The downstream proof also loses its roundabout subtract-and-simplify recovery of a fact proved upstream, so it is shorter and less fragile under `simp` changes. Readers of either file can see that both arguments rest on the same continuity fact.
